nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-01.title: Match the first card
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-01.body:
Whatever the first card is, $3$ of the remaining $51$ cards have the same rank. So the probability is $\frac{3}{51}=\frac1{17}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1}{17}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-01.title: Count pairs
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-01.body:
There are $\binom{52}{2}=1326$ two-card hands and $13\binom42=78$ pairs, so the probability is $\frac{78}{1326}=\frac1{17}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1}{17}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-02.title: Least common multiple
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-02.body:
Adding $14$ keeps divisibility by $14$ unchanged, so the number itself is divisible by $14$, by $8$ and by $18$, hence by $\operatorname{lcm}(14,8,18)=2^3\cdot3^2\cdot7=504$. The only 3-digit multiple of $504$ is $504$.

**Answer: 504**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-03.title: Sum of odd numbers
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-03.body:
$1+3+\cdots+(2n-1)=n^2$, so the first $100$ odd integers sum to $100^2=10000$.

**Answer: 10,000**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-03.title: Pair them up
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-03.body:
Pair $1$ with $199$, $3$ with $197$, and so on: $50$ pairs each summing to $200$, giving $10000$.

**Answer: 10,000**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-04.title: Add rates
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-04.body:
Together they paint $\frac1{10}+\frac1{15}=\frac{3+2}{30}=\frac16$ of the room per hour, so they need $6$ hours.

**Answer: 6 hours**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-05.title: Coordinates
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-05.body:
Put the vertex at $(0,0)$ and the square at $[0,1]^2$. The midpoints are $(\frac12,0)$, $(0,\frac12)$, $(1,\frac12)$, $(\frac12,1)$. The distances are $\frac12,\frac12,\sqrt{1+\frac14}=\frac{\sqrt5}2,\frac{\sqrt5}2$, totalling $1+\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $1+\sqrt5$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-06.title: Rate per cow
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-06.body:
One cow gives $\frac{B}{AC}$ cans per hour, so $D$ cows give $\frac{BD}{AC}$ cans per hour. To give $E$ cans they need $E\div\frac{BD}{AC}=\frac{ACE}{BD}$ hours.

**Answer: $\frac{ACE}{BD}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-07.title: Arithmetic sequence
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-07.body:
If he earns $a$ on day $1$, the week totals $7a+5(0+1+\cdots+6)=7a+105=259$, so $a=22$.

**Answer: \$22**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-07.title: Middle day
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-07.body:
The average day is the 4th day: $\frac{259}{7}=37$. The first day is $3\cdot5=15$ less: $22$.

**Answer: \$22**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-10.title: Closing the gap
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-10.body:
By 2:30 P.M. David is $2.5\cdot40=100$ miles ahead. His wife gains $60-40=20$ miles per hour, so she needs $\frac{100}{20}=5$ hours: 7:30 P.M.

**Answer: 7:30 P.M.**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-12.title: Stars and bars
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-12.body:
We need $a+b+c=6$ with each at least $1$ (and automatically at most $4$): $\binom52=10$ ordered outcomes out of $216$. Probability $\frac{10}{216}=\frac{5}{108}$.

**Answer: $\frac{5}{108}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-13.title: Right triangle
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-13.body:
The radius is $10$, and the chord is at distance $5$ from the centre. Half the chord is $\sqrt{100-25}=5\sqrt3$, so the chord is $10\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $10\sqrt3$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-14.title: Divisibility by 8 and 3
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-14.body:
$P^2-1=(P-1)(P+1)$. As $P$ is odd, $P-1$ and $P+1$ are consecutive even numbers, one divisible by $4$, so $8\mid P^2-1$. As $P$ is not divisible by $3$, one of $P-1,P+1$ is divisible by $3$. So $24\mid P^2-1$. It is the largest such number since $11^2-1=120$ and $13^2-1=168$ have $\gcd(120,168)=24$.

**Answer: 24**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-15.title: Track the acid
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-15.body:
The solution has $2.4$ oz of acid. Adding $x$ oz of acid: $\frac{2.4+x}{24+x}=0.4$, so $2.4+x=9.6+0.4x$, $0.6x=7.2$, $x=12$.

**Answer: 12 ounces**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-15.title: Track the water
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-15.body:
The water, $21.6$ oz, never changes. In the final $40\%$ solution water is $60\%$, so the total is $\frac{21.6}{0.6}=36$ oz; John adds $36-24=12$ oz.

**Answer: 12 ounces**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-16.title: Remainder theorem
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-16.body:
The remainder is the value at $x=-1$: $1-1-1=-1$.

**Answer: $-1$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-17.title: Multiply the factors
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-17.body:
The value is multiplied by $1.1^3\cdot0.9^2=1.331\cdot0.81=1.07811$, a gain of $7.811\%$.

**Answer: $7.811\%$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-17.title: Pair the days
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-17.body:
Each up-down pair multiplies by $1.1\cdot0.9=0.99$. Two pairs give $0.9801$, and Friday's rise gives $0.9801\cdot1.1=1.07811$: a $7.811\%$ gain.

**Answer: $7.811\%$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-19.title: Smallest P2 first
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-19.body:
Make $P_2$ as small as possible. $P_2=2$ gives $124$ (not prime); $3\to123=3\cdot41$; $5\to121=11^2$; $7\to119=7\cdot17$; $11\to115$; $13\to113$, which is prime. So $P_1-P_2=113-13=100$.

**Answer: 100**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-21.title: Median to the hypotenuse
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-21.body:
$M$ is the midpoint of hypotenuse $AB$, which is the centre of the circumcircle, so $MC=MB$. Triangle $CMB$ is isosceles with $\angle MCB=\angle B=40^\circ$, so $\angle CMB=180^\circ-80^\circ=100^\circ$.

**Answer: $100^\circ$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-23.title: Count negatives
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-23.body:
Each $\frac{a}{|a|}$ is $\pm1$, and the last term is their product. If $m$ of $a,b,c,d$ are negative, $K=(4-2m)+(-1)^m$: $m=0\to5$, $m=1\to1$, $m=2\to1$, $m=3\to-3$, $m=4\to-3$. So $K\in\{-3,1,5\}$.

**Answer: $-3,\ 1,\ 5$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-25.title: Halve repeatedly
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-25.body:
$[ABD]=\frac12[ABC]=12$ since $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$. $[EBD]=\frac12[ABD]=6$ since $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$. $[FBD]=\frac12[EBD]=3$ since $F$ is the midpoint of $BE$. Finally $[DGF]=\frac12[FBD]=\frac32$ since $G$ is the midpoint of $BD$.

**Answer: $\frac32$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-26.title: Factor
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-26.body:
$xy-x-y+1=1$, i.e. $(x-1)(y-1)=1$. The integer factorizations of $1$ are $1\cdot1$ and $(-1)(-1)$, giving $(x,y)=(2,2)$ and $(0,0)$.

**Answer: $(0,0)$ and $(2,2)$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-27.title: Exterior angles
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-27.body:
Each exterior angle is $180^\circ-170^\circ=10^\circ$, and they sum to $360^\circ$, so there are $36$ sides.

**Answer: 36**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-28.title: Sequential
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-28.body:
The second card matches the first's suit with probability $\frac{12}{51}$, and the third with $\frac{11}{50}$: $\frac{12\cdot11}{51\cdot50}=\frac{132}{2550}=\frac{22}{425}$.

**Answer: $\frac{22}{425}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-29.title: Alternating sum
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniorb-29.body:
From the right, the alternating digit sum is $0-8+1-4+K-9+2-8+3-5+2-7=K-33$. It must be a multiple of $11$, and $33$ already is, so $K=0$.

**Answer: 0**
